mainTopic: Sealed doorways, public rights of way, minimum sizes for dividing shared property, and נבואה remaining with the חכמים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about sealed doorways. As long as the doorframe stands, the doorway still counts, both for the ארבע אמות in front of a house and for where טומאה goes out. Once the frame is broken out, the doorway is gone. Next, רבי יוחנן and שמואל teach that the public keeps its right to pass through alleyways it already uses. This holds even when another road exists, and it covers the whole alley, not just the first four אמות. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's minimum sizes for dividing shared property: a field, a cistern, an orchard, and a vineyard. For each of these it also gives the local measure used in בבל. רבי יוסי's remark that סומכוס's measure is 'words of prophecy' opens a discussion about נבואה. The discussion teaches that after the חורבן, נבואה stayed with the חכמים, and that a חכם is greater than a נביא. אביי brings a proof for this, רבא rejects it, and רבא begins his own proof, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A sealed house keeps its four cubits unless the doorframe is broken
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a house with a sealed doorway still gets its ארבע אמות, but once the doorframe is broken out it loses them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A house whose doorway is sealed still has its four cubits. If someone broke out its doorposts, it no longer has the four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us when a sealed doorway still counts as a doorway for getting the ארבע אמות in front of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply blocking a doorway does not erase it, because the doorframe is still there and the door could easily be reopened. Once the פצימים (doorposts) are broken out, the doorway is completely gone. Then the house loses the extra space it would get in front of that entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: four cubits: the space in front of a doorway that the house gets
doorposts, the frame of a doorway

steps.confusionAlert: A sealed doorway is NOT the same as a doorway with a broken-out frame. As long as the frame is still standing, the doorway still counts even though it is blocked.

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת סָתוּם – יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת;
phrases.english: A sealed house has four cubits;
phrases.notes: He means a house whose doorway was blocked up, with the doorframe still standing.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַץ אֶת פַּצִּימָיו – אֵין לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: if he broke out its doorposts, it does not have four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיִת סָתוּם – יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from earlier in the daf about the ארבע אמות that a doorway gets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed doorway with its frame intact still earns ארבע אמות; once the doorposts are broken out, it does not.

steps.title: The same idea with a sealed grave and טומאה
steps.stepSummary: A grave with a sealed entrance does not spread טומאה all around it, but if its doorposts were broken out and it was sealed, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A grave whose entrance is sealed does not make everything around it impure. If someone broke out its doorposts and then sealed it, it makes everything around it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a matching rule from the laws of טומאה, using a grave as the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the doorframe is still there, the entrance still counts, so the טומאה goes out only through that opening. When the frame was broken out and the space was sealed, there is no doorway at all. The טומאה then spreads out on every side.

keyTerms.meaning: everything around it, on all sides

phrases.english: A grave whose entrance is sealed –
does not make everything around it impure;
if he broke out its doorposts and sealed it –
it makes everything around it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same test as Step 1 (is the doorframe still standing?), now for טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed grave entrance with its frame intact limits where the טומאה goes; once the frame is broken out, the טומאה spreads on all sides.

steps.title: The same rule for a house with a dead body inside
steps.stepSummary: A house containing a dead body, with a sealed doorway, does not spread טומאה all around it. Once its doorposts are broken out, it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sealed house does not make everything around it impure. If someone broke out its doorposts, it makes everything around it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the same טומאה rule for a house that has a dead body inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as the grave in Step 2. With the frame still there, the doorway still counts and controls where the טומאה goes. Without the frame, there is no doorway, so the טומאה spreads in every direction.
steps.whatToRemember: In all of these cases, a blocked doorway still counts as long as its frame (פצימים) is standing. Breaking out the frame removes the doorway completely, whether we are talking about ארבע אמות or טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת סָתוּם – אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא כׇּל סְבִיבָיו;
phrases.english: A sealed house does not make everything around it impure;
phrases.notes: Here the house has a dead body inside it.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַץ אֶת פַּצִּימָיו – מְטַמֵּא כׇּל סְבִיבָיו.
phrases.english: if he broke out its doorposts, it makes everything around it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיִת סָתוּם – אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא כׇּל סְבִיבָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the grave rule from Step 2 to a house, which finishes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sealed house doorway with its frame intact limits where the טומאה goes; once the doorposts are broken out, the טומאה spreads on all sides.

steps.title: Residents may not block alleyways that lead to another city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if alleyways lead through to another city, the people of that other city can stop the local residents from blocking them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If alleyways open through to another city, and the residents of this city want to block them, the residents of that other city can stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the public's right to keep using a passageway it depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The alleyways belong to one city, but people from the other city travel through them. Because of this, the people of the other city have a say. They can block the local residents from closing the alleyways.

keyTerms.meaning: that open through, leading out on the other side

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Alleyways that open through to another city,
and the residents of the city wanted to block them –
the residents of that city can stop them.
phrases.notes: "That city" means the other city, the one the alleyways lead to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, separate from the ברייתא about sealed doorways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The residents of the other city can stop the local residents from blocking alleyways that lead through to their city.

steps.title: This applies even when there is another road
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's rule holds even when the other city's people have a different route available.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not needed to say that they can stop them when there is no other road. Rather, even when there is another road, they can also stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies how far רבי יוחנן's ruling reaches, and sets up the reason that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the other city only has a claim if it has no other way to get through. The גמרא says that case is obvious. The new point is that they can object even when another road exists. This shows the right does not depend on need, which is why the גמרא now looks for a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not needed to say, it is obvious

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיבְּעֵי כִּי לֵיכָּא דַּרְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא – דִּמְעַכְּבִי,
phrases.english: It is not needed to say that when there is no other road, they can stop them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ כִּי אִיכָּא דַּרְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: but even when there is another road,
they can also stop them –

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיבְּעֵי כִּי לֵיכָּא דַּרְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 4 to the less obvious case where another road exists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The other city can stop the blocking even if they have another way to travel.

steps.title: The reason: a public path may not be ruined
steps.stepSummary: The reason is רב's ruling that a path the public has taken hold of may not be ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because of what רב יהודה said in the name of רב, who said: A path that the public has taken hold of may not be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for why the other city can object even when it has another road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the public has established its use of a path, it gains a lasting right to that path. That right does not depend on whether the public truly needs it. So blocking the path ruins something that already belongs to the public.

keyTerms.meaning: a path, a strip of land
took hold of, established use of
to ruin it, to make it unusable

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule about public rights of way. When the public uses a path, it gains a real right in it that the owner cannot take away.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: Because of what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav, who said:
A path that the public has taken hold of,
it is forbidden to ruin it –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the rule in Step 5 holds even when another road exists.
steps.raayaObject: That the other city can stop the blocking even when it has another road.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that a path the public has taken hold of may not be ruined.

steps.title: רב גידל: what the public chose stays chosen
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling fits with רב גידל, who says that a path the public chose for itself stays theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רב גידל, as רב גידל said: If the public chose a path for itself, what they chose is chosen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב's ruling matches the teaching of רב גידל, which finishes the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל teaches that the public's choice of a route sets up a permanent right. That is exactly why the public's established path cannot be ruined. So the people of the other city keep their right to use the alleyways.
steps.whatToRemember: Once the public establishes a route, it keeps that right for good. That is why the other city can stop anyone from blocking the alleyways, even if it has another road.

phrases.english: Like Rav Giddel, as Rav Giddel said:
The public that chose a path for itself –
what they chose, they chose.
phrases.notes: He means their choice sticks: the path stays theirs and cannot be taken away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties רב's ruling from Step 6 to רב גידל's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a public path may not be ruined.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב גידל: a path the public chose for itself stays theirs.

steps.title: The public can stop alley residents from putting up doors
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן in the name of שמואל: if alleyways open onto a רשות הרבים, the public can stop the alley residents from putting doors at the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said in the name of שמואל: Alleyways that open through to a public area, where the alley people want to put up doors, the people of the public area can stop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל that fits the theme of the last few steps. The public has rights in an alley that opens onto a public area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is like רבי יוחנן's ruling about alleys that lead to another city (Step 4). Here it is the general public on the main road who can block the doors. The idea is that the public has already been using the alley as a way through.

keyTerms.meaning: Alleyways, small side streets with houses
Open through at both ends, so people can pass through
Public area, a main road used by everyone

phrases.english: Rav Anan said in the name of Shmuel:
Alleyways that open through onto a public area,
and the residents of the alleyways wanted
to set up doors for themselves,
the people of the public area can stop them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling on public rights in alleys, continuing the theme of רבי יוחנן and רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Users of the public area can block alley residents from installing doors at an alley that opens onto the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Some thought the rule covers only the first four cubits
steps.stepSummary: Some understood that שמואל's rule applies only within four אמות of the public area, based on רבי זירא quoting רב נחמן that those four אמות count as a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some understood from this that it applies only within four cubits, like רבי זירא said in the name of רב נחמן: the four cubits next to a public area are treated like the public area.
steps.whatsHappening: Some people suggest a limit on שמואל's ruling. They bring רב נחמן's rule as support. The גמרא is setting this up so it can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the public only has a claim where the alley counts as public property. Since רב נחמן says only the first four אמות count as public, they suggest the public could only stop doors in that area.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first impression that may be rejected)
They are like, they are treated as

steps.confusionAlert: This is only what some people first thought. The גמרא will reject it right away with ולא היא, so do not take it as the final ruling.

phrases.english: Some understood from this
that this applies only within four cubits,
phrases.notes: That is, the four cubits of the alley closest to the main road.

phrases.english: in line with what Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Nachman:
The four cubits next to the public area
are treated like the public area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a limit on שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The proposed limit of שמואל's rule to the first four אמות
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא in the name of רב נחמן: the four אמות next to a רשות הרבים are like the רשות הרבים

steps.title: Rejection: crowds can push deep into the alley
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the four-אמות limit. רב נחמן spoke about טומאה, but crowds on the main road sometimes push far into the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There it was about טומאה. But here, sometimes the people of the public area get crowded and go in much farther.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from the last step. It shows that רב נחמן's rule was about a different subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאה only the first four אמות count as public. But the public's right of way is about how people actually use the alley, and a crowd can spill deep inside. So the public can block doors anywhere in the alley.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so (rejects an idea)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule covers the whole alley, not just the first four אמות. A rule from the area of טומאה does not automatically carry over to property rights.

phrases.english: But that is not so.
There, it was about ritual impurity,
phrases.notes: "There" means רב נחמן's rule about the four cubits.

phrases.english: but here,
sometimes the people of the public area get crowded,
and they go in much farther.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the four-אמות limit suggested in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב נחמן's rule to limit שמואל's ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן's rule was about טומאה, while public passage depends on real crowd movement, which can reach deep into the alley.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the minimum size for dividing a field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a shared field is not divided unless each partner gets room for nine קבין of seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And not a field, unless it has nine קבין for this one and nine קבין for that one, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a new line of the משנה about dividing a shared field. It is setting up its comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field is measured by how much seed it takes to sow it. One partner cannot force a split unless each share is still big enough to be a real field. The "and so on" points to רבי יהודה's smaller size, nine half-קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב is a measure of volume; here, the amount of seed a piece of land can take

phrases.english: And the court does not divide a field

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין לָזֶה,
phrases.english: unless it has room for nine kav of seed for this one,
and nine kav for that one, and so on.
phrases.notes: "And so on" points to the rest of the משנה, where רבי יהודה says nine half-kav is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּהּ תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the alleyway topic to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shared field is divided only if each share can take nine קבין of seed (רבי יהודה: nine half-קבין).

steps.title: They do not really argue: each followed his own place
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה do not truly disagree. Each gave the size that counted as a field in his own place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not argue. This Sage ruled by his place, and that Sage ruled by his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two different sizes in the משנה. It says this is not a real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the rule: a share must be big enough to be called a field where you live. They only differ on numbers, because in רבי יהודה's area even a smaller plot was a usable field.

keyTerms.meaning: This Sage according to his place (local custom)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the measure depends on local custom. That sets up the next question: what is the size in בבל?

phrases.english: And they do not argue.
This Sage ruled by his place,
and that Sage ruled by his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two measures quoted from the משנה in Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה seem to argue about the minimum size of a field.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold the same rule. Each gave the size that was a usable field in his own area.

steps.title: What is the size in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: Since the size depends on the place, the גמרא asks what counts as a field in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: In בבל, what is the size?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that follows from the last step. It wants the measure for בבל, where it is being studied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sizes in the משנה were given for ארץ ישראל. Since the size follows local custom, the measure in בבל could be different.

phrases.english: In Babylonia, what is the rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the local-custom idea of Step 12 to בבל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of a dividable field in בבל

steps.title: רב יוסף: a day's plowing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that in בבל a field is the area that can be plowed in one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The area of a day's plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. In בבל, the measure of a field is how much land you can plow in one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of measuring by seed, בבל measures by a day of plowing. If each partner would get less than that, the field is not split.

keyTerms.meaning: The area plowed in one day

steps.whatToRemember: The size needed to divide a field depends on local custom. In ארץ ישראל it was nine קבין (or nine half-קבין), and in בבל it is a day's plowing for each partner.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The area of a day's plowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בֵּי רָדוּ יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In בבל, the minimum share is the area that can be plowed in one day.

steps.title: Which day of plowing is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'a day's plowing' means. Plowing in the planting season and plowing in the plowing season take different amounts of time, and either choice seems to cause a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the area of a day's plowing'? If it means a day of plowing in the planting season, then in the plowing season it will not come out to two full days. If it means a day of plowing in the plowing season, then in the planting season it will not come out to a full day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's measure from the last step. 'One day of plowing' is not a fixed size, because plowing goes faster or slower depending on the season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker is hired by the day. If the field is measured by the easy season, then in the hard season the job takes more than one day but less than two, so a partner pays for two days and gets less work. If it is measured by the hard season, then in the easy season the job takes less than a full day, so a day's wage is again partly wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: The area that can be plowed in one day
It does not come out to (it is not enough)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the size of the field. The problem is that a day's work is not a full day's work in every season, so a hired worker's day is partly wasted.

phrases.english: What is 'the area of a day's plowing'?
If it means a day of plowing in the planting season,
then it will not come out to two days in the plowing season;
phrases.notes: In the plowing season the ground is hard, so the work takes longer, but not twice as long.

phrases.english: if it means a day of plowing in the plowing season,
then it will not come out to a full day in the planting season!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בֵּי רָדוּ יוֹמָא״? אִי יוֹמָא זַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the measure רב יוסף just gave.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's definition of a field in בבל as 'a day's plowing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: whichever season sets the measure, the field will not fit a whole number of work-days in the other season.

steps.title: Two ways to make the plowing measure work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two answers. It may mean the plowing season, since in the planting season he plows twice. Or it may mean the planting season, since on rocky ground the plowing season really takes two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it means a day in the plowing season, because in the planting season he plows and then plows again. And if you want, say it means a day in the planting season, and the case is rocky ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two different ways. Each answer shows that the measure does fit a whole number of work-days in both seasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: if the measure is the plowing season, the planting season still fills a full day, because he plows before sowing and plows again after. Answer two: if the measure is the planting season, rocky ground makes the plowing-season work take a full two days.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces one possible answer)
He plows and repeats (plows a second time)

phrases.english: If you wish, say it means a day of the plowing season,
because he plows and then plows again;
phrases.notes: In the planting season he plows once before sowing and once after, so it still fills a whole day.

phrases.english: and if you wish, say it means a day of the planting season,
and it is talking about rocky ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative answers, each showing the other season also fits whole days
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either choice of season leaves a partial, wasted work-day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra second plowing, or the rocky ground, fills out the time exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: The field measure in בבל, 'a day's plowing,' stands. Either answer shows it fits real work-days.

steps.title: Minimum share for splitting a cistern
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a shared cistern is split only if each partner gets enough water for a day's irrigation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A cistern: רב נחמן said, it must hold enough for a day of drawing water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item: the minimum share needed to divide a shared cistern. רב נחמן gives the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the field, the cistern is measured by its practical use. Each share must be big enough to water fields for one full day. If it is smaller, the partners cannot force a split.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern or water pit used for irrigation
Enough for one day of drawing water

phrases.english: A cistern: Rav Nachman said:
enough for a day of drawing water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the field to a related item: dividing a cistern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cistern is divided only if each share holds a day's irrigation water.

steps.title: Minimum share for splitting an orchard
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל rules that an orchard is split only if each partner gets an area for three קבין of seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orchard: שמואל's father said, an area of three קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more minimum size, this time for an orchard. אבוה דשמואל says each share must be three קבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An orchard needs only a third of the nine קבין required for a field. A smaller piece of orchard is still useful, so the minimum is lower.

keyTerms.meaning: An area large enough to plant three קבין of seed

phrases.english: An orchard: Shmuel's father said:
an area of three kav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item (an orchard) to the list of minimum shares.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orchard is divided only if each share is an area for three קבין of seed.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports three קבין for a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports אבוה דשמואל. סומכוס says someone who sells 'part of a vineyard' must give at least three קבין. רבי יוסי says this figure seems to come from nowhere, like 'words of prophecy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: if someone tells his friend, 'I am selling you part of a vineyard,' סומכוס says he may not give less than three קבין. רבי יוסי said: these are only words of prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same three-קבין size for a vineyard. This backs up אבוה דשמואל's number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס treats three קבין as the smallest piece that counts as 'part of a vineyard.' That matches the orchard measure. רבי יוסי objects that the seller never named a size, so setting one seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)
Words of prophecy: a ruling with no clear reason behind it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not praising סומכוס. 'Words of prophecy' means he sees no logical basis for the number.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
one who says to his friend:
'I am selling you a portion of the vineyard' —
Sumakhos says:
he may not give less than three kav.
Rabbi Yosei said:
These are nothing but words of prophecy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for אבוה דשמואל's three-קבין orchard measure.
steps.raayaObject: אבוה דשמואל's ruling of three קבין for an orchard
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which סומכוס sets three קבין as the minimum for 'a portion of a vineyard'

steps.title: What is the orchard measure in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the matching vineyard or orchard measure is in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: In בבל, what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as it did with the field, the גמרא asks for the local measure in בבל. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sizes depend on local custom, as the גמרא showed with the field. So the three-קבין figure may not be how people in בבל measure a vineyard.

phrases.english: In Babylonia, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the local measure, like the field question in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of an orchard or vineyard share in בבל

steps.title: In בבל: three rows of twelve vines
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר קסנא answers that in בבל the measure is three rows of twelve vines each, which is what one man can hoe in a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר קסנא said: three rows of twelve vines each, which is what a man can hoe in one day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר קסנא gives the measure used in בבל. Like the field, it is based on one day's work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size is set by what one worker can hoe in a day: three rows of twelve vines. This matches רב יוסף's 'one day's plowing' for fields in בבל.
steps.whatToRemember: In בבל, shares are measured by one day's work: a day's plowing for a field, and a day's hoeing (three rows of twelve vines) for a vineyard.

phrases.english: Rava bar Kisna said:
three rows of twelve vines each,
which is what a man can hoe in a day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three rows of twelve vines, which is one man's day of hoeing.

steps.title: Prophecy moved from the prophets to the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבדימי דמן חיפה says that since the חורבן, נבואה was taken from the נביאים and given to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבדימי from חיפה said: From the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, prophecy was taken away from the prophets and given to the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: Because רבי יוסי just called סומכוס's measure 'words of prophecy,' the גמרא brings a statement about where נבואה went after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבדימי claims that after the חורבן, נבואה did not disappear completely. It moved into the hands of the חכמים. This sets up the whole discussion that follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed,
prophecy was taken from the prophets
and given to the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side discussion triggered by רבי יוסי's phrase 'words of prophecy' in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, נבואה passed from the נביאים to the חכמים.

steps.title: Isn't a Sage also a prophet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: it sounds as if a חכם and a נביא are totally separate people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that a Sage is not a prophet?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to how רבי אבדימי worded his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying נבואה was taken 'from the נביאים' and 'given to the חכמים' suggests two separate groups. But many נביאים were also great חכמים, so the wording seems off.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? A question showing surprise

phrases.english: Is that to say a Sage is not a prophet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי אבדימי's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבדימי's phrasing that splits נביאים and חכמים into two groups.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חכם can be a נביא too, so it makes no sense to say נבואה was moved from one group to the other.

steps.title: Prophecy stayed with the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אבדימי means נבואה was taken from the נביאים but not from the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: even though prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by re-reading רבי אבדימי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבואה was not handed over to a new group. Rather, the חכמים, who already had some of it, kept it, while the נביאים lost theirs.

phrases.english: This is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה מִן הַנְּבִיאִים,
phrases.english: Even though it was taken from the prophets,
from the Sages it was not taken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23 by explaining the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבואה was moved from one group, the נביאים, to a different group, the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים always had it and kept it. Only the נביאים lost theirs.

steps.title: A Sage is greater than a prophet
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says a חכם is greater than a נביא, because the פסוק compares the נביא to wisdom, and the lesser is always compared to the greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: A Sage is even greater than a prophet, as the פסוק says, 'And a prophet has a heart of wisdom.' When one thing is compared to another, which is compared to which? The smaller is compared to the bigger.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר goes a step further and ranks the חכם above the נביא, bringing a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the נביא by comparing him to wisdom. Since you always describe the lesser thing by comparing it to the greater one, wisdom must be the greater quality.

keyTerms.meaning: Is compared to, is described by

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
And a Sage is greater than a prophet,
as it says: "And a prophet has a heart of wisdom" —
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:12. The גמרא reads the word וְנָבִא as 'and a prophet.'

phrases.english: who is compared to whom?
You must say: the lesser is compared to the greater.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 24: the חכמים not only kept נבואה, they are even greater than נביאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם is greater than a נביא, learned from the פסוק 'ונבא לבב חכמה.'

steps.title: אביי's proof: two great men reach the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that חכמים still have a kind of נבואה: one great חכם states a ruling, and the same ruling is reported from another great חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can see this is true, because a great man says something, and then the very same thing is reported in the name of another great man.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof from real life that the חכמים still have a kind of נבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great חכמים, each on his own, arrive at the exact same ruling. אביי says this shows that their rulings come from a kind of divine help, not just from reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is so); an opening for a proof
A great man, a great חכם
Like him, the same as his

phrases.english: Abaye said: Know (that this is so),
for a great man says something,
and it is said in the name of
another great man, just like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for רבי אבדימי's claim, as explained in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the חכמים still have a kind of נבואה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that two great חכמים, separately, reach the identical ruling.

steps.title: רבא: maybe they share the same מזל
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's proof: the two חכמים may simply have been born under the same מזל, so they think alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What kind of proof is that? Maybe both of them were born under the same מזל, so they naturally think the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people born under the same מזל have similar natures and minds. So reaching the same ruling may come from thinking alike, not from נבואה, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? Meaning, this is easy to explain otherwise
מזל, the star sign one is born under

phrases.english: Rava said: And what is the difficulty?
Maybe both of them
were born under the same מזל!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's proof is rejected, not the idea that חכמים have נבואה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The matching rulings can be explained by a shared מזל, without any נבואה.

steps.title: רבא begins his own proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a better proof that the חכמים have a kind of נבואה, again about a great man's ruling being reported. The rest continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: You can see this is true, because a great man says something, and it is reported...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up רבא's own proof, which is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having rejected אביי's proof, רבא offers his own. It opens the same way, but it will need a case that a shared מזל cannot explain.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is said, it is reported

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: Know (that this is so),
for a great man says something,
and it is said...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where רבא finishes his proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected proof with רבא's own proof.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the חכמים still have a kind of נבואה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A great man's ruling that matches a ruling reported elsewhere; the details follow on the next part of the daf.
